title: ～切れない — cannot finish, cannot fully ～
summary: Means one cannot do something to the end because the amount or degree is too large. It attaches to a verb stem.

patterns.form: Vます形（ます抜き）＋切れない

body.p: 切る here means 'to the end,' so its negative potential 切れない means 'cannot do it to the end': 食べ切れない, 使い切れない, 数え切れない, 言い表し切れない. The positive ～切れる also exists.
It covers not only physical amounts but also feelings and degrees that cannot be fully expressed: 信じ切れない, 言い表し切れない. 数え切れないほど means 'so many one cannot count.'

examples.ja: 料理（りょうり）が多（おお）すぎて食（た）べ切（き）れない。
examples.tr: There's too much food; I can't finish it all.

examples.ja: お店（みせ）には数（かぞ）え切（き）れないほどの商品（しょうひん）が並（なら）んでいる。
examples.romaji: Omise ni wa kazoekirenai hodo no shōhin ga narande iru.
examples.tr: The shop has more products than one can count.

examples.ja: この一年（いちねん）の思（おも）い出（で）は言葉（ことば）では表（あらわ）し切（き）れない。
examples.romaji: Kono ichinen no omoide wa kotoba de wa arawashikirenai.
examples.tr: I can't fully put this year's memories into words.

pitfalls: Do not keep ます: 食べ切れない, not 食べますきれない.
This 切る is not 'to cut'; it means 'to do to the end.'
